hints: Recall the relationship between power, driving force, and speed: $P = F_D \times v$. Remember to convert 8 kW into Watts.
Since the crate moves at constant speed, the net force parallel to the inclined plane is zero: $F_D - mg\sin\theta - F_{\text{friction}} = 0$.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane to find the normal reaction: $R = mg\cos\theta$.
Use the limiting friction law $F_{\text{friction}} = \mu R$ and solve for $\mu$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force exerted by the winch using $P = F_D \times v$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{8000}{2} = 4000\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane to find the normal reaction force $R$:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 600(10)\cos 30^\circ = 6000\cos 30^\circ = 3000\sqrt{3}\approx 5196.15\text{ N}$$

Apply equilibrium of forces along the line of greatest slope at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - mg\sin 30^\circ - F = 0$$
$$4000 - 600(10)\sin 30^\circ - F = 0$$
$$4000 - 3000 - F = 0 \implies F = 1000\text{ N}$$

Use the friction relationship $F = \mu R$ to determine the coefficient of friction $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{1000}{6000\cos 30^\circ} = \frac{1}{6\cos 30^\circ} = \frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\approx 0.192$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Start by stating the formula connecting power, pulling force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Convert the winch power from kilowatts to watts: $P = 8\text{ kW} = 8000\text{ W}$. Rearrange the formula to isolate the pulling force $F_D$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Substitute the numerical values $P = 8000\text{ W}$ and $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{8000}{2} = 4000\text{ N}$$

Next, consider the forces acting on the 600 kg crate perpendicular to the inclined plane. The plane is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Since there is no acceleration perpendicular to the incline, the normal contact force $R$ balances the perpendicular component of the crate weight:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ$$

Substitute $m = 600\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 600 \times 10 \times \cos 30^\circ = 6000\cos 30^\circ\text{ N}$$

Now, resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane. The crate moves up the slope at constant speed, so its acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), which means the resultant force along the slope is zero:
$$F_D - mg\sin 30^\circ - F_{\text{friction}} = 0$$

Finally, because the crate is sliding, friction is at its maximum (limiting) value given by:
$$F = \mu R$$

Divide both sides by $R$ to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{1000}{6000\cos 30^\circ} = \frac{1}{6\cos 30^\circ}$$
